public_rationale: Independent research available before the post showed image generators memorizing and reproducing training images. A separate study identified copying through comparisons with source images. This supports the ordinary technical reading of regurgitation. The evidence does not establish that copying dominates normal use, occurs equally often in image and text models, or necessarily constitutes copyright infringement.
limitations: The result depends on reading prone as demonstrated susceptibility rather than a specified high frequency.
Model versions, prompts, and extraction methods affect the findings.
The attribution to Marcus and Southen is not independently adjudicated.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Generative image programs are prone to the same kind of regurgitation of copyrighted material as text models.

statement.excerpt: And what Southen and I showed is that generative image programs are prone to exactly the same kind of regurgitation that is at issue.
statement.document_title: The desperate race to save Generative AI

from_speaker: exactly the same kind of regurgitation
our_interpretation: The plain reading is that image generators have a demonstrated susceptibility to reproducing existing source images, comparable to text models reproducing source passages.
Near-copies must preserve identifiable source content; similarity of style alone does not qualify.
The comparison concerns the kind of failure, not equal reproduction rates across image and text models.

The observation concerns capabilities demonstrated by the post date. These systems have no regular reporting period, and the retrospective wording supplies no starting date, so the target period has an unspecified start.
This assesses the technical phenomenon, not whether a particular output legally infringes copyright or whether Marcus and Southen first discovered it.
criteria.support_condition: Independent experiments on image generators available before the post document reproduction of identifiable training images or substantial source content, using source comparisons and described methods.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Independent examination shows that the purported reproductions are merely stylistic similarities, supplied input images, or retrieval results, and credible tests fail to substantiate generation of identifiable source content.

evidence.explanation: The experiment establishes generation of memorized training images. This directly supports the technical meaning of regurgitation, without establishing infringement or a typical-use frequency.
A separate research team compared generated images with training samples and identified copying in Stable Diffusion. This corroborates the phenomenon independently of Marcus and Southen.

evidence.excerpt: typically is only possible for very few samples.
evidence.explanation: This limits a stronger reading that image generators routinely reproduce arbitrary training images. It does not negate demonstrated susceptibility.
